description: I'm Sarah, the leader of the group.
summary:
Space Museum is an interactive virtual museum that brings the human-made artifacts left on the Moon and Mars to life. We catalogued seven artifacts, four on the Moon and three on Mars, using NASA archives and official sources. They are the Apollo lunar module descent stages, the Lunar Roving Vehicle, the ALSEP science stations, the lunar laser retroreflectors, the Perseverance and Curiosity landing hardware, and the InSight lander. Each one gets a visual exhibit and a short story-driven narrative that explains what it did, where it rests, and what it left behind.

The project answers the challenge “Abandoned but Not Forgotten” by showing that these objects are not scrap. They are lasting records of science and engineering. Some, like the laser reflectors, still work today. Others, like InSight, left behind data that continues to teach us about their worlds.

It matters because it makes space history accessible and engaging for everyone, and it inspires curiosity about the people and machines behind exploration.
details: What it does and how it works Beyond Earth: The Space Museum is a bilingual (English/Arabic) interactive website. It works as a virtual museum of seven human-made artifacts left on the Moon and Mars. The site has five sections: Collection, Overview, Comparison, Sources, and Team. Visitors browse the Moon and Mars collections as exhibit cards and open any artifact to see its official name, mission, date, location, scientific or engineering function, how it was used, why it was left behind, its importance, and its current status. A comparison table lines the artifacts up side by side. Every artifact lists its NASA-based sources and image credit. The story “A Journey Through the Space Museum” links the seven exhibits into one guided narrative. Benefits It turns scattered archive material into one organized, easy-to-read experience. It reframes “abandoned” objects as lasting records, and the laser reflectors are still in use today. Arabic and English versions, with right-to-left layout, reach a wider audience. Every fact links back to a source, so it is easy to check. Intended impact We want students, teachers, and the general public to see space history as a story of science and engineering that continues after a mission ends. We hope it inspires curiosity, and the same structure can be extended with more artifacts or languages. Tools and technology HTML, CSS, and JavaScript in a single self-contained file, with no external libraries, so it runs offline and loads easily. Embedded images, and a data-driven design: all artifacts and translations live in JavaScript data objects that generate the pages. Responsive layout for mobile screens. Microsoft Word, PowerPoint, and PDF for the research report, story, and presentation. UI/UX design in [WPS Office / your design tool]. Sources: NASA archives, NASA History, LROC, JPL, and the Smithsonian NASM. [Add any AI tools your team used, as the competition may ask you to disclose them.] Creativity Storytelling replaces a dry catalogue: a night-time museum visit with a guide who narrates each station. The museum is built around the challenge theme, “Abandoned but not Forgotten”. The collection mixes active exhibits (laser reflectors), retired ones (InSight), and “supporting cast” hardware (landing equipment), which gives visitors surprises along the way. The data analysis set the display priority: laser reflectors first, then the Apollo 11 descent stage, InSight, and the landing hardware (“seven minutes of terror”). Factors we considered Accuracy: facts come from official NASA sources, and each artifact has its own source links. Accessibility: two languages, readable text, and mobile support. Audience: a non-expert public, so content is short and story-led. Image rights: the site notes that photos are NASA media and that each archive page should be confirmed. Teamwork: data, writing, design, and development were split across roles so each part could proceed in parallel. Scope: we limited the collection to seven artifacts to keep the quality high.
